摘 要 及 調 整 原 因 
➢ 缺料影響營運不如預期，下修 Q3獲利預估，EPS 9元 
➢ HVDC滲透率提升，且持續海內外擴產，2027 年營收挑戰超越 1兆元，EPS 62.3元。考量
電源產業將進入全新格局且台達作為主要先行者將最為受惠，兆豐投顧維持目標價 2000 元
(約 32X 27(F)PER)，潛在上漲空間 19.8%，建議逢低買進。

- 2 - 
個股報告 
資料來源：CMoney；兆豐投顧預估

營 運 分 析

台達電為全球電源管理及散熱解決方案領導廠商 
台達電(2308)成立於 1971 年並於 1988 年掛牌上市，成立初期分別投入生產
交換式電源供應器與無碳刷式直流風扇，目 前已取得全球電源產品龍頭地
位。2017 年公司啟動組織調整，以「電源及零組件」、「自動化」、「基礎
設施」、「交通」四大業務範疇，並從傳統關鍵零組件製造商逐步轉型為節
能解決方案提供者。近年隨AI 資料中心建置需求爆發，公司積極將既有電源
技術延伸至 AI伺服器電源機櫃、液冷 side car、BBU、DC-DC/AC-DC模組
及 CDU 等新產品線，目前終端應用已從傳統 NB/工業電源、資料中心跨足
至高壓供電(HVDC)與液冷散熱系統，客戶涵蓋NVIDIA與北美 CSP及 ASIC
供應鏈。

26Q2 營收比重:(1)電源及零組件 53%,包含電源、被動元件等零組件、風扇
散熱;(2)交通 5%,電動車解決方案;(3)自動化 8%,包含工業自動化,樓宇自動
化;(4)基礎設施 34%,包含資訊通訊技術(通信電源、網通交換器、資料中心
解決方案、液冷side car)、能源基礎設施(電動車充電樁、可再生能源及儲能
設備等)。受惠 AI 資料中心電源需求與規格持續提升，台達持續擴充台灣、
中國大陸、泰國與美國產能，並同步推進 800V HVDC 架構開發，全面迎接
NVIDIA 新世代 GPU 機櫃功耗大幅提升所帶動的電源與散熱升級需求。

- 3 - 
個股報告

缺料影響營運不如預期，下修 Q3獲利預估，EPS 9 元 
台達電(2308)公告 8月營收：營收 645.9 億元，MoM -3.7%/YoY +34.9%，
Q3達成率 62.4%，低於研究部預期與市場共識，係因 MOSFET 全產品線呈
現缺料所致，故研究部下修台達電 26Q3 營收 1960.8 億元(原估 2,107.4 億
元)，QoQ +7.0%/YoY +30.4%，而先前 18.3KW PSU 因電容問題有進行產
品召回，不過預期本月將處理完畢且對財務無任何影響；毛利率方面，受惠
產品組合轉佳與規模經濟抵銷原料/電子元件漲價影響，預估毛利率 35.8%，
仍可維持與上季相當，季增 0.2ppt，反映營收下修，同步下修稅後淨利 232.6
億元，QoQ -7.5%/YoY +25.0%，EPS 9元(原估 10.5 元)。

AI 電源與散熱產品持續放量，輔以新產品推出，2026 EPS 37元 
展望 2026 年，主要成長動能仍來自 AI 資料中心電源、散熱與基礎設施，在
電源方面隨著 GB300 持續放量與 H2 VR200之 18.3KW 產品開始出貨，預
期價量齊揚挹注營運動能，此外 HVDC(±400V/800V)產品於 3Q26 開始量
產，惟在初期階段預期僅小幅貢獻；在散熱產品方面(涵蓋水冷板、Manifold、
CDU及 Sidecar)在 2026 下半年可望延續成長動能，主要受惠液冷滲透率持
續提升與內容價值同步墊高。綜上所述，反映 Q3下修，同步下修台達電 2026
年營運預估：2026 年營收 7,465.4 億元，YoY +34.5%，毛利率 36.2%，年
增 1.9ppt，稅後淨利 960.8 億元，YoY +59.8%，EPS 37.0元（原估 40 元）。

HVDC滲透率提升，且持續海內外擴產，2027年營收挑戰超越 1兆元，EPS 
62.3元 
展望 2027 年，受惠 CSP業者 CAPEX 持續增長，公司為滿足訂單需求，持
續加大投資力道，2026 年資本支出約 700 億元(YoY +50%)，資金來源除自
有資金外，9/15 公告發行泰達電可交換公司債籌措 15 億美元以滿足擴產資
金需求，2027 年也可望維持高檔水準，預計於泰國、中國、台灣與美國同步
擴產，研究部認為 HVDC(±400V/800V)較大規模量產貢獻有望於 2027 年起
顯現，同時液冷、電源機櫃、DC-DC模組等新產品線持續放量，此外公司亦
持續推進 SST 與 SOFC 等能源基礎設施長期布局，電源產業將迎來新格局
與長期成長動能。兆豐投顧預估台達電 2027 年營收 1.1 兆元，YoY +43.0%，
毛利率 37%，年增 0.8ppt，稅後淨利 1617.6 億元，YoY +68.4%，EPS 62.3
元。

   公司簡介 
強茂為台灣功率半導體與分離式元件製造大廠，公司採垂直整合佈局，擁有 3 座前段

買進 208 
【 前 次 投 資 建 議 】區 間 操 作，150

➢ 2Q26 獲利符合預期 
強茂 2Q26 營收 39.56 億元，QoQ+15.62%，YoY+16.34%，毛利率
33.22%， 稅後淨利4.88 億元 ，QoQ+69.58%，YoY+93.85%，EPS 1.28
元，獲利大致符合預期。毛利率維持季增趨勢，但營業費用比預期高，
主因是客戶拉貨強勁，備貨及物流相關費用多及提列獎金所致。 
➢ 下半年營收、獲利逐季向上 
AI 伺服器、車用及小訊號產品訂單能見度佳，強茂 B/B ratio 值維持在
1.3~1.5 高檔位置，3Q26 新增部份產能，加上產品調漲，預期營收及毛
利率持續向上；4Q26 有機會切入另一家 CSP 供應鏈，年底增加封測產
能(小訊號為主)、越南 TOREX 預計在 1Q27 交割，整體而言營運動能無
虞。預估強茂 3Q26 營收 42.51 億元，QoQ+7.47%，YoY+30.02%，
毛利率 34.44%，稅後淨利 5.58 億元，QoQ+14.39%，YoY+84.08%，
EPS 1.46 元。 
➢ 歐美重心轉移、非紅供應鏈，台 IDM 廠有訂價權 
在 AI 需求強勁推動下，單機櫃功耗持續上升並導入高壓直流電架構，帶
動功率元件量價同步提升，應用於伺服器功率元件年複合成長率遠高於
產業平均，在產能吃緊情況下，歐美 IDM 廠將重心轉向利潤較佳的高
壓、SiC 以及低壓大電流的 DrMOS 核心市場，排擠中低壓功率元件產
能。同時，安世、揚傑等中資背景企業面臨去中化，伺服器、車用工控
等領域加速將訂單轉向台廠。 
➢ 預估強茂 2027 年 EPS 6.95 元，建議買進，目標價 208 元 
投研部預估強茂 2026 年營收 159.39 億元，YoY+21.73%，稅後淨利
19.21 億元，YoY+61.22%，EPS 5.03 元；預估 2027 年營收 183.38 億
元，YoY+15.05%，稅後淨利 26.57 億元，YoY+38.29%，EPS 6.95 元。
目前強茂 PE 24X ，2026 年最高本益比已超越 2017~2018 年、
2020~2022 年功率元件景氣循環 20X~30X 區間，AI 伺服器的應用有
助拉升功率元件產業及公司評價，給予強茂買進建議，目標價 208 元
(2027F PE 30X)。

個股報告

公司簡介 
強茂股份有限公司成立於 1986 年，為台灣功率半導體與分離式元件製造大廠，公司
採垂直整合(IDM)佈局，擁有 3 座前段晶圓製造廠(4 吋、6 吋、8 吋各一座)，及 5 座
海內外後段封裝測試據點。 
1H26 產品營收比重 ： 金氧半場效電晶體(MOSFET)佔 32%， 蕭特基二極體(Schottky)
佔 23%，整流器(Rectifier)佔 12%，突波抑制器(TVS)佔 9%，靜電防護二極體(ESD 
Diode)佔 7%，齊納二極體(Zener)佔 6%，開關二極體(Switching)佔 6%，雙極性接
面電晶體(BJT)佔 4%，碳化矽(SiC)佔 1%。若以市場應用來看，車用電子佔營收比重
35%為最大，消費型電子佔 20%，電腦運算佔 16%，工控&綠能佔 13%，電源供應
用佔 12%，通訊佔 4%，其中 AI 人工智能應用佔 11%。

- 3 -

個股報告 
下半年營收、獲利逐季向上 
AI 伺服器、車用及小訊號產品訂單能見度佳，強茂 B/B ratio 值維持在 1.3~1.5 高檔
位置，強茂 8 月營收 13.76 億元，MoM-4.89%，YoY+29.82%，3Q26 新增部份產
能，加上產品調漲，預期營收及毛利率持續向上，4Q26 有機會切入另一家 CSP 供應
鏈，年底增加封測產能(小訊號為主)、越南 TOREX 預計在 1Q27 交割，整體而言營運
動能無虞。預估強茂 3Q26 營收 42.51 億元，QoQ+7.47%，YoY+30.02%，毛利率
34.44%，稅後淨利 5.58 億元，QoQ+14.39%，YoY+84.08%，EPS 1.46 元。 
歐美重心轉移、非紅供應鏈，台 IDM 廠有訂價權 
在 AI 需求強勁推動下 ， 單機櫃功耗持續上升並導入高壓直流電架構 ， 帶動功率元件量
價同步提升，應用於伺服器功率元件年複合成長率遠高於產業平均，在產能吃緊情況
下，歐美 IDM 廠將重心轉向利潤較佳的高壓、SiC 以及低壓大電流的 DrMOS 核心市
場，排擠中低壓功率元件產能。同時，安世、揚傑等中資背景企業面臨去中化，伺服
器、車用工控等領域加速將訂單轉向台廠。 
目前成熟製程與後段封裝產能極度吃緊，具備晶圓代工、晶片設計到封裝完整布局的 
強茂等 IDM 廠，憑藉產品線的廣度及垂直整合優勢，能確保供貨不中斷並免受外包
產能排擠 ， 更實質掌握了稀缺產能的訂價權 ， 在這一波由AI 架構升級與地緣政治雙軌
驅動的轉單潮中，將成為優先且最大受惠者。 
機櫃功率愈大，功率元件量價同步提升 
AI 應用佔強茂營收比重 11%，多數來自運算托盤(compute tray)上 Power MOSFET、
Schottky、TVS 或小訊號等功率產品，運算托盤上功率元件產值佔整機櫃超過一半，
主要核心在整合式供電模組(DrMOS)，DrMOS 技術門檻高，由歐美大廠主導，台廠
不易切入，但供電相數的增加，將同步提升對周邊功率元件的需求量。 
以 GB300 為例，單顆 GPU 功率 1.4kW，電壓 0.8V，核心負載輸出電流是 1,750A，
根據單顆高密度 DrMOS / SPS 晶片的最大承載電流(70A~130A)規格去設計供電相
數(Power Phase) ，每一相數都必須配置一套完整的硬體元件，當 GPU 功率提升至
2.3kW (Vera Rubin) ，GPU 功率增加 60%，供電相數及功率元件需求量亦將等幅放
大。 強茂功率元件已成功打入CSP 大廠 ， 未來將持續受惠運算托盤上功率元件量的提
升及質的改變(如 TVS 相對大電流，晶粒面積變大，單價提升)，產業成長趨勢明確。 
預估強茂 2027 年 EPS 6.95 元，建議買進，目標價 208 元 
投研部預估強茂 2026 年營收 159.39 億元，YoY+21.73%，稅後淨利 19.21 億元，
YoY+61.22%，EPS 5.03 元；預估 2027 年營收 183.38 億元，YoY+15.05%，稅後淨
利 26.57 億元，YoY+38.29%，EPS 6.95 元。目前強茂 PE 24X，2026 年最高本益比
已超越 2017~2018 年、2020~2022 年功率元件景氣循環 20X~30X 區間，AI 伺服
器的應用有助拉升功率元件產業及公司評價， 給予強茂買進 建議，目標價 208 元
(2027F PE 30X)。

展望 2026年，完工案量與前一年相當，憑藉優異銷售策略與品牌
聲量，住宅案已全數完銷，商辦則持續與潛在買方洽談中，若期限
內未能找到整棟購置客戶，將改採分層銷售模式，預計年底前去化
約 50%，後續若順利完成整棟出售，則不排除上修獲利預估。展
望後市，公司持續獵地推案，目前建案能見度至 2034年，銷售中
總銷逾千億元，待推出總銷逾 900 億元，顯示公司中長期業績成
長無虞，惟短期受房市景氣及銷售速度放緩影響，業績表現仍存在
不確定性。股利方面，公司過往現金股利最低配發5元，且現金股
利配發率長期維持 70~80%，推估 2027 年現金股利有望達 6~7
元。綜合以上，研究部預估 2026、2027年 EPS 7.28、9.78元，
以 1.4*PBR評價，給予目標價 111元，投資建議為買進。 
 近期投資評等  營運概況 
1H26 營收 57.07億元，YoY+181.4%，稅後損益 9.43 億元，
YoY+307%，EPS 2.92 元，略低於研究部預期。上半年營收
主要來自新案「華固上文林」持續交屋挹注，全案總銷 61 億
元，已順利於8M26 完成過戶。獲利方面，1H26 毛利率 27%，
YoY-5.8ppt，由於新推案土地成本較高，加上興建期間物料及
工資上漲，導致利潤率略低於預期。

 公司展望 
展望 2026 年 ， 全年將迎來三大建案完工交屋 ， 合計總銷為179
億元，YoY-2.8%，分別為「華固一莊」(總銷 41 億元，完銷，
8M26 交屋)、「華固上文林」(總銷 61 億元，完銷，1H26交
屋)、「華固時代置地」(總銷 77 億元，持續與潛在客戶洽談
整棟出售，若期限內未能找到整棟購置客戶，公司將改採分層
銷售模式，預計年底前去化約 50%)。獲利方面，住宅案因土
地成本墊高，個案毛利率應介於25~26%之間；商辦產品則因
市場降溫，成交價格與利潤率回歸合理水準，毛利率預估約
28~30%，使全年合併毛利率將較 2025 年下滑，預估為
26.8%，YoY-1.43ppt。綜合以上，研究部預估 2026 年營收
140.85 億元， YoY-22.77%，稅後損益 23.27 億元，
Yo-28.21%，EPS 7.28元。

展望 2027 年，預計有三大建案完工交屋，合計總銷為205 億

「華固芙心」 總銷53 億元，銷售率95~100%、 「華固四季匯」
總銷 54 億元，銷售率35~40%、「華固譽誠」總銷54 億元，
銷售率 85~90%、「華固創匯園區」總銷 325 億元，銷售率
25~30%。

2027年公司將再推出 「央北二案」(總銷64億元 ， 單價105~110
萬/坪，總價 4~5 千萬)、「松勇路案」(總銷 70億元，250 萬
/坪，2~3 億/戶，合計總銷為 134 億元，預計於 2030~2031
年完工交屋。

市況方面，2H24 起國內房市受限貸令及信用管制措施影響，
台中地區產品銷售速度趨緩，雙北地區則相對穩健，因此公司
未來獵地方向將回歸雙北，並以 60%住宅+40%廠辦為目標。
隨房市移轉量及房價已明顯降溫，因此央行近期放寬第二戶貸
款成數至 7 成，有助於提振換屋需求及購屋信心，最壞情況已
過，整體銷售動能有望回溫。

土地庫存方面，尚有逾 900 億元待推案將陸續於 2027~2030
年推出，並於 2034 年前完工挹注，顯示公司中長期業績成長

AI semi capex, in particular for compute chips, should outgrow
overall AI capex in 2028. We add cross-checks on ASICs after
AVGO’s guidance and the Qualcomm/AWS AI ASIC
announcement.
Will 2028 be another growth year for AI semis? Our US internet analyst Brian
Nowak published the Morgan Stanley AI Guidebook: Navigating the Age of
Inference, and suggests 12% CSP capex growth into 2028, raising investor questions
about AI semi growth momentum. Based on our latest supply chain checks, we

introduce preliminary 2028 CoWoS/CoPoS/EMIB-T capacity assumptions. In
aggregate, we still see 50% capacity growth in 2028 (see Exhibit 1), implying
flattish infrastructure (e.g., the shell and AI DC) spending and moderate memory
pricing in 2028.
Larger chip size and more applications (CPU, networking) to drive further
growth in 2028: All these packaging technologies are 2.5D (compute and memory
chips on side to side) for AI/HPC chips, including AI GPU, XPU, CPU, and networking.

•CoWoS (wafer based): We still see some CoW expansion at TSMC. For oS, TSMC
may need more partners than ASE. Our checks suggest both Amkor and Xintec
(non-covered) will diversify oS production in the US and Taiwan, respectively.
• CoPoS (panel-based): This is a panel-level process. After converting to 12-inch
CoWoS wafer equivalents, we assume 5–10kwpm in 2028. The initial target project
should be Nvidia’s Feynman Ultra GPU.
• EMIB-T (substrate-based): Although a substrate-based technology, we convert it

to 12-inch CoWoS wafer-equivalent capacity as well. One EMIB-T substrate can
generate 16 pcs of a 9x reticle-size chip, around 4x the chips a CoWoS wafer can
generate. Our checks indicate ~40k–45k wafer-equivalent EMIB-T capacity in 2028,
producing at least 2mn of Humufish (9x reticle) substrates. 40k–45k wafer
equivalents also imply 10-15% share in 2.5D packaging.
Read-across from recent ASIC guidance at Broadcom and the Qualcomm/AWS
partnership

•According to Joe Moore’s report: Broadcom Inc.: Earnings solid; raising FY 28 EPS,
more specific FY27 revenue guidance is now US$115 bn, and that could double again
in FY28. Our CoWoS supply-chain checks already see an AVGO AI lab customer
booking ~15k–30k CoWoS wafers for 2027.
•Qualcomm announced its ASIC partnership with AWS, a key Alchip ASIC customer.
However, the press release points to inference, different from Alchip’s Trainium4,
which covers both training and inference. We therefore see limited impact to Alchip.

communications with a subject company, public appearances
and trading securities held by a research analyst account.

TSMC CoWoS and CoPoS
With continual booming demand in AI, we expect TSMC and its OSAT partners to expedite
capacity expansion plans for CoWoS. We expect TSMC's CoWoS capacity to further build
to 260kwpm in 2028 from 130/200kwpm in 2026/2027, with 2028's expansion mainly

focusing in Arizona's AP9/10 and potentially in AP7. TSMC is now conducting trial
production for CoPoS in Taoyuan. As long as the progress goes well, we expect TSMC to
start building its CoPoS capacity, with the location also likely to be in AP9/10 or AP7P3.
We expect the non-TSMC camp to expand CoWoS capacity to 110kwpm by 2028 year-end
from 80kwpm by end-2027. For ASE/SPIL, we expect FoCoS+CoWoS capacity to rise from
30kwpm at 2027-end to 50-60kwpm at 2028-end, with expansion focused on CoWoS-L

and CoWoS-R. For Amkor, we expect CoWoS capacity to increase from 30kwpm at 2027-
end to 55-60kwpm at 2028-end, also focused on CoWoS-L and CoWoS-R.

For Intel, we see current average EMIB-M capacity being 110kwpm, which would slightly
decrease to 95kwpm in 2027 as it's converting some capacities toward EMIB-T. We see the
major customers of EMIB-M being Trainium3, upcoming Trainium 4 and its in-house server
CPU. Average EMIB-T capacity is around 5kwpm in 2026, which we expect to further scale
to 15-20kwpm in 2027 and 40-45kwpm in 2028. All of the capacity mentioned above is
converted for  12-inch wafer equivalent, which we believe would be much more easier to

communicate and compared with TSMC CoWoS capacity.
Although some small projects are ongoing, we still see MediaTek/Google Humufish
consuming most of the capacities during 2027-28. We maintain our view that Intel EMIB-T
could still  produce close to 3mn units of Humufish from late 2027-2028, by assuming 4-5
chips per wafer of EMIB-T.

• AMD's total 2027 CoWoS consumption increases 165% Y/Y to 345k:
° We expect AI GPU-related production to be all at TSMC CoWoS, while

series (chip code name Arcadia) in late 2027. Both MI455 and MI450 could
reach around 500-650k units respectively. We estimate total TSMC CoWoS-L
booking increases 200% Y/Y in 2027, to 210k.
° We see the non-TSMC camp, including ASE/SPIL and  Amkor, being mainly in

charge of Venice CPU, high-end PC CPU, and gaming GPU production.

### Page 3

Earnings revision: We factor in SZS Aug revenues, revise down 2026E earnings by 11%, 
revise up 2027E earnings by 1%, and keep 2028E earnings largely unchanged. We revise 
down 2026E revenues mainly on lower-than-expected Aug revenues, considering longer 
time for new projects to reflect on company’s revenues/ earnings. We revise up 2027 
earnings mainly on higher revenues, reflecting our positive view on SZS as the key 
beneficiary of rising foldable phones.

Valuation: We are Buy rated on SZS with a 12-month target price of NT$300 (vs. 
previously at NT$286) on lower earnings. Our TP is based on a 21.9x 2027E P/E (vs. 
previously at 21.0x), which is derived from the updated sector correlation of 2027E P/E 
vs. 2027E-28E EPS YoY (Exhibit 8), with re-rating supported by positive view on rising 
foldable phone penetration. The 21.9x 2027E P/E is also within SZS’s trading range since 
Aug 2019.

### Page 4

Price Target Risks and Methodology - SZS 
Valuation: We use a near-term P/E vs. EPS growth correlation to derive our target price 
for SZS, consistent with our Taiwan Technology coverage. Our target 2027E P/E multiple 
of 21.9x for SZS is based on the sector correlation of 2027E P/E vs. 2027-28E earnings 
growth. We thus derive our 12-month target price at NT$300. We are Buy rated. Key 
risks: Weaker-than-expected headset hinges demand; slower-than-expected foldable 
phone penetration; potential competition from more suppliers; soft market demand.

## Document 079: 260914_gs_optical-tour

Source PDF: all report pdf/260914_gs_optical-tour.pdf
Report source: line報告備份
Date: 2026-09-14
Pages: 9
Extraction status: ok

### Page 1

1. Optical module demand outlook: Companies we visited remain positive on 
optical module demand, driven by AI server racks ramp up, optical module adoption 
expansion (from scale out to scale up / across), and specification upgrade. On global 
market demand on 800G and 1.6T, demand could be at 130m to 200m; for the China 
market, overall demand could also grow at mid double digits to 50m+ units, with the 
majority 800G and 400G, and 1.6T emerging. Nevertheless, companies we visited 
with also mentioned that tight raw material supply (e.g. DSP , lasers, PCB) could 
continue to cap shipments in 2027. The positive tone echoes our positive view on 
global demand, on which we raised 800G and above optical module demand by 39% 
/ 36% in 2027E / 2028E to 144m / 171m (report link). Supply chain positive tone 
reflects further upside to our estimates. 
2. Optical module competition: Companies we visited see pricing competition 
remaining healthy, with 800G optical module pricing decline within single digits in 
2027, and 1.6T optical module price to sustain at US$700+. Managements highlight 
that optical module is not a pure assembly but with multiple SKUs and require 
suppliers’ strong R&D and timely development as compared to telecom, the product 
cycle could shorten to 1-2 years in datacom vs. 5 years in telecom. Supply chain 
management and mass production capability are also important to win orders, 
especially under the current tight supply situation and clients’ requirements of 
diversifying production sites under geopolitical tension. Innolight, as the global 
leader works with supply chain closely, including R&D collaboration, invests directly 
in their suppliers, and pre-payment and long-term agreements to secure a

### Page 2

sustainable supply through cycles.
3. Laser supply: Chinese suppliers are ramping up capacity and capability in 200G EML,
supporting the 1.6T optical module ramp up in 2027. Nevertheless, shipment also
depends on other raw material supply (e.g. DSP), and customers penetration.
Everbright‘s laser capacity prepared for 2027 is EML slightly higher than CW laser, and
within the EML majority is for 100G, with the remaining for 200G; Dongshan Precision

highlights their 200G EML is already in mass production, while volume is still small
currently given the tight supply of DSP; nevertheless, the company also secured 10m
supply of DSP in 2027, supporting their lasers and optical modules shipment ramp up.
VPEC, global leading InP epiwafer supplier, also sees improving InP substrate supply, with
steady export permission from China government, more customers bringing InP
substrate, and growing second to fourth suppliers outside of China. VPEC’s MOCVD is

also in expansion, from current 62 MOCVD to 69 MOCVD by 2Q27, and planning a new
production site in 2027.
4. CPO timeline: As a new technology, CPO will naturally take time and could face
challenges in the path of commercialization. For example, laser suppliers see thermal
challenges for 300mW / 400mW CW lasers in ELS (external laser source), and is working
on 100mW+ with PA for NPO first. Optical module suppliers also see strong 3.2T NPO
optical engine demand across China and overseas markets. Nevertheless, equipment

suppliers remain the earliest beneficiary in CPO, with the strong testing and coupling
demand reflecting in equipment suppliers’ revenues in mid 2026. For example,
Robotechnik 2Q26 revenues were up 172% QoQ, or 141% higher than our estimates. As
we highlighted in Sep (report link), we estimate CPO switch at 10k / 92k / 131k units in
2026E-28E.
5. AI spending sustainability: Management highlighted that AI is a revolution, and we
are at an early stage of infrastructure spending and application development. It will be a

long cycle for the coming 10 to 20 years, and some of their customers are planning
beyond 2030. The demand for the coming 2 to 5 years remains very strong and
management highlighted their industry enjoys short return on investment, which is
around 1 to 2 years. Management highlighted the AI spending is not only building more
AI data centers, but also includes technology migration, such as making power
consumption more efficient, making data transmission faster, etc., driving the supply

chain growth. Compared to the internet bubble in the 2000s, management sees much
more transparency between end-customers (demand) and supply chain (supply), as end
customers are involved more in supply chain product development and capacity
investment, reducing the information gap between demand and supply, and reducing
the chance of double booking. Management noted that currently every module they
produce is being deployed in data centers, reflecting real demand.

6. Photonics IC scaling up: AI drives data transmission speed and bandwidth
requirement, leading to strong demand on Photonics IC, requesting it to catch up
Electrical IC automated production and testing ecosystem in 1 to 2 years, while EIC /
semiconductors has been developed for decades. The strong demand brings
opportunities to tool suppliers, across coupling and testing, which are necessary tools to
accelerate PIC production. Robotechnik / FiconTEC describes the number of tools they

target to ship in the coming 1 year would be over 50% of what they’ve shipped in the
past 25 years, reflecting the strong demand and orders visibility.
14 September 2026   2
Goldman SachsFor the exclusive use of KEVINLU@LENOVO.COM

### Page 3

7. Testing - CPO earliest beneficiary: As a new technology, CPO naturally takes time
and faces challenges in the path of commercialization; however, we identify testing
equipment suppliers as the earliest beneficiaries, considering the expensive final module
means multiple testing during the production process is necessary, given the earlier a
failure is found, the lower cost a failure is. As a result, companies we visited continue to
see Insertion 2 (double-sided wafer-level testing) as necessary, and Robotechnik /

FiconTEC launched the new generation in 3Q26, which fully complied with the global
leading foundry’s communication infrastructure.
8. Testing - shortening time with KGD (know good die) at early stage: To facilitate
photonics IC scaling up, not only are more tools needed but better tools, requiring
suppliers’ strong R&D and execution, delivering continuous specification upgrade.
Robotechnik / FiconTEC, as global leaders in PIC testing, aim to shorten the wafer-level

testing time by 50-60% next year, and target 4x faster die-level testing next year.
Enlitech (7728.TWO, Not Covered) offers NightJar, a hyperspectral image system,
revealing AWG (arrayed waveguide grating) optical loss pathways with absolute optical
power mapping, allowing customers to KGD at Insertion 1 (PIC wafer testing) or Insertion
0 (PIC wafer early defect screening), saving failure costs.
9. Coupling - automated production becoming necessary in high-speed connection:

AI drives optical module towards high speed and high density / bandwidth, driving
demand on automated production. GMT (4573.TWO, not covered) showcased dual FA
active alignment equipment for 1.6T optical module, which could do the coupling for
both Tx and Rx simultaneously, saving 50% of coupling time compared to traditional
equipment. FitTech (6706.TW, not covered) has showcased an optical engine assembly
system, featuring passive / active alignment and customized development of coupling

algorithms, which could be used in multiple products: high-speed optical modules, ELS,
OCS, NPO, CPO, SiPh and optical chiplets. ASMPT has showcased MEGA multi-chip
bonding solution for complex multi-chip and photonics packaging applications,
combining high-precision placement with adhesive dispensing, UV fixation and 3D
inspection in one platform.
10. FAU & Laser specification upgrade: With optical networking expanding from scale
out to scale up, FAU and laser specification is also migrating. FOCI‘s FAU in 2026 to be

mainly 40 channels (starting in 3Q26) for 3.2T, followed by 80 channels (within 2026) for
6.4T, and 100 channels under R&D, per management. The company’s FAU enjoys several
customers across fabless, foundry, laser suppliers, etc. FOCI Aug revenues accelerated to
+20% MoM (vs. +9% MoM in Jul), reflecting the ramp up of high-end FAU. VPEC‘s
optoelectronics revenues enjoy strong growth on the back of strong CW lasers demand
and InP substrate supply getting better. Its InP epiwafer for CW lasers is also migrating

from 70mW / 100mW (scale out) to above 100mW (scale up, NPO) and 300mW /
400mW (scale up, CPO), along with expansion from CW lasers to 100G / 200G EML,
supporting its growth ahead.

Price Target Risks and Methodology - Zhongji Innolight Co.
Valuation: Our 12-m TP for Innolight A-share of Rmb2,645 is based on 35.6x 2027E P/E,
and our 12-m TP for Innolight H-share of HK$3,267 is based on a H-A premium of 13%.
We derive our target P/E multiple from the networking peers’ trading P/E vs.
forward-year fundamentals (NI YoY and OPM). Compared to Innolight’s historical trading
range, the target multiple reflects our view of its leading market position in high-speed

connections and product-mix upgrade toward SiPh optical modules, driving GM
expansion. We are Buy rated.
Key downside risks: 1) slower-/worse-than-expected 800G+ optical modules demand;
2) slower/worse-than-expected new optical devices ramp pace; 3)
faster-than-expected market share normalizing in 800G+ optical modules; 4)
geopolitical risks; and 5) worsening component supply situation to constrain shipment
growth.
Price Target Risks and Methodology - VPEC

Valuation: We adopt a discounted P/E method and apply a 22.2x target P/E on VPEC’s
2029E EPS, discounting back to 2027E at a COE of 10.5% (beta 1.7x, risk free rate 1.6%
and market risk premium at 5.1%), to derive our 12m TP of NT$793. Our target P/E is
based on a 0.4x PEG&M ratio derived from the average level of peers in the photonics
supply chain.
Key risk: Slower-than-expected SiPh business ramp up; weaker-than-expected
microelectronics demand from smartphones clients; IDM offers EPI wafer in-house.

Price Target Risks and Methodology - RoboTechnik
Valuation: Our 12-month target price of Rmb796 is based on a 20.7x 2031E P/E,
discounted back to 2027E at a COE of 11.3%. Our target multiple is derived from the
correlation between consumer electronic peers’ PEG&M (2026E P/E to 2027E NI YoY and
OPM), with RoboTechnik’s 2032E net income at 2% YoY and 2032E OPM at 32%.
Key downside risks: Fiercer-than-expected market competition; lower-than-expected

optical connection end demand; worse-than-expected photovoltaic market downcycle.
Valuation: Our 12-month target price of NT$833 is based on a 15.4x 2030E P/E,
discounted back to 2027E at a COE of 12.6%. Our target multiple is derived from peers’
correlation between forward-year trading P/E and earnings growth.
Key downside risks: Fiercer-than-expected market competition, technology migration
trends in optical networking, and slower-than-expected capacity ramp-up.

Price target methodology and risks - ASMPT
Valuation methodology: We are Neutral rated on ASMPT with a 12-month target price
of HK$177, which is based on a 24.9x 2030E discounted P/E (discounted back to 2027E).
Our target P/E is derived from correlation between peers P/E to the sum of NI YoY and
OPM.
Key upside/downside risks: 1) customers’ faster-/slower-than-expected adoption of
Advanced Packaging tools; 2) stronger-/weaker-than-expected demand from

automotive customers; and 3) stronger-/weaker-than-expected demand for traditional
IC packaging and SMT equipment.

### Page 1

UMT provides rectangular waveguides, which are conducting pipes with a 
rectangular cross-section used to guide the propagation of microwave or mmwave 
signals. Different shapes and combinations of waveguides can form various RF 
passive components, such as filter / diplexer, coupler, isolator, antenna, power 
amplifiers (PAs), etc. The company serves leading global LEO satellite operators, and 
its waveguides can be seen in LEO satellites / payloads (main), and gateways in 
ground stations.

### Page 2

LEO satellite launches update: Starlink launched 261 LEO satellites in Aug 2026, or 
+13% MoM. The number of satellites per launch continues to increase from 24 satellites 
per launch in May 2026 to 26 satellites per launch in Aug 2026, and at 27 satellites per 
launch so far in Sep 2026, reaffirming our positive view on the constellation construction 
cycle. On Sep 18, SpaceX’s Starship V3 is scheduled to have the 3rd flight and the first 
Starship flight to deploy satellites (a group of Starlink satellites) into stable LEO, and 
should have the 4th flight of Starship V3 within 2026 (link). Starship V3 is a reusable 
vehicle, with LEO capacity at 100k kg, or 339% higher than Falcon 9 Block 5 (22.8kg), the 
current vehicle that Starlink is using. The vehicle migration would not only accelerate 
Starlink’s satellite launches but also release the legacy vehicle (e.g. Falcon 9 Block 5) to 
other LEO satellite operators, facilitating the overall industry’s satellite launches. For 
example, Amazon has planned 10 launches (LF-04 to LF-13) in 2029, using Falcon 9 
Block 5. Assuming 27 satellites per launch via the vehicle, the 10 missions would bring 
270 satellites (vs. 180 / 216 satellites in 2025 / 7M26 that Amazon added). Amazon is 
also increasing its satellites per launch: the upcoming pipeline shows 35-48 satellites per 
launch vs. 29-36 satellites per launch in May to July 2026, or increasing by 28% on avg. 
The acceleration of LEO satellite launches reaffirms our positive view on UMT.

Earnings revision: We factor in Aug revenues, and raise net income by 1% in 2026-28E. 
The revenue raise is to reflect our positive view on accelerating LEO satellite launches 
along with specification upgrade driving up the dollar content. Our GM is reduced to 
reflect our expectation that the larger scale would lead to lower GM with customers’ 
rising procurement power. Nevertheless, with the company’s product mix upgrade 
toward LEO satellite, the blended GM should continue to increase through 2028E.

Valuation: We continue to derive our target price based on a discounted P/E, and based 
on 2029E (methodology unchanged). We continue to derive the target P/E multiple from 
the average PEG&M ratio of peers in the satellite supply chain, and we remove outliers 
(those below 0.3x, which are mostly telecom operators who face competition from LEO 
satellite operators or having consumer electronics exposure which suffered from high 
memory costs). Our target 2029E discounted P/E multiple is at 37.0x (unchanged) which 
is based on peers’ avg. PEG&M, and UMT’s 2029-30E avg. NI YoY and OPM. We apply the 
37.0x multiple to 2029E EPS and discount it back to 2027E via a COE of 7.8% (no 
change). Our target price is at NT$2,557 (vs. NT$2,513 previously), implying 61x 2027E 
P/E, which is above the company’s average +1 stv. P/E of 42x, reflecting our positive view 
on UMT’s product mix upgrade toward LEO satellites. Maintain Buy.

Price target risks and methodology - UMT 
Valuation: We use a discounted P/E methodology and apply a 37.0x target P/E multiple 
to UMT’s 2029E EPS, discounting it back to 2027E at a COE of 7.8% (beta 1.2x, risk-free 
rate 1.6% and market risk premium at 5.1%), which leads to our 12-month target price 
of NT$2,557. The target P/E is based on the average PEG&M ratio of peers in the 
satellite supply chain. We are Buy-rated on UMT.  
Key Risks: Slower-than-expected LEO satellite deployment; Potential competition from 
new-entrant suppliers; LEO satellite operators manufacturing in-house components.

First Read
Delta Electronics
Add to APAC Key Call Buy - Taiwan Summit
reaffirms the AI Power opportunity
Capturing a robust industry TAM as the leading server power supplier
Delta affirmed a stronger growth profile as AI infrastructure now is over 50% of sales.
Our bottom-up model from our APAC Focus (link) estimates a 69% CAGR to US$91.1bn
AI server power TAM from 2025-2030 even moderating 2028-30 for hyperscale cash

flow and grid power constraints. We see a strong 2027 driven by +65% YoY accelerator
die growth, Rubin's ~60% higher rack power and AMD's move to rack-scale systems.
400V/800V becomes a larger driver in 2028-29 as rising power density outgrows low-
voltage distribution. We believe Delta is key beneficiary with its  broad grid-to-chip
portfolio helping sustain its ~40% share of a rising TAM.
Near-term supply constraints bottoming from Aug and accelerating into Q4.

Supply constraints on Power ICs have tempered Q3 growth from +15-20% QoQ to +10-
12% QoQ but should grow in Sep and accelerate to double digit QoQ in Q426 and
above seasonal Q127 (UBS +3% QoQ) into new ASIC/GPU platform ramps and more
supply. Management expects shortages to persist for at least the next several quarters
with demand accelerating faster than supply and the supply-demand gap likely
widening before narrowing but price hikes rebounding OpMs.

HVDC Adoption Appears Increasingly Inevitable.
HVDC production and shipments have begun and should be modest in 2027 before
ramping sharper in the following 1-2 years. As rack power rises from 140kW on GB300
to nearly 250kW on VR200 and potentially higher on Rubin Ultra, management expects
space and efficiency constraints to shift power systems out of racks and into side-car or
centralized architectures. Delta sees HVDC as the logical solution for power-loss,

thermal, and density challenges, with higher-voltage architectures offering multiple-
times higher value per watt than current solutions. Delta sees three hyperscalers
evaluating 400V, two adopting it for NVIDIA racks initially before converging on 800V.
Reiterate Buy and PT NT$2,750
Delta's stock has pulled back 36% since May following push-outs to NVIDIA's
architecture slowing the dedicated power rack ramp-up and elevating supply
constraints, pulling it back to 22x/17x 2026-27 EPS. We now see better entry with sales

ramping in H226, spec upgrades to ASIC power racks and Rubin at 60% higher TDP over
Blackwell and margins holding better than feared. The company should leverage its
strong product line, R&D and field support to participate in the key power architecture
transitions in the coming years moving the power stack out of the rack and also
developing emerging nascent technologies including SST for facility level power
transformation and rectification and fuel cells licensing Ceres for medium-term

opportunity to supplement the power grid constraint with alternative energy.

Company Description
Delta Electronics provides computer switching power supply solutions, as well as video display
and electronics components, for computers, smartphones, telecom and industrial products.
Founded in 1971, the firm has production bases in Taiwan, China, Thailand and India. In

2023, its power electronics, infrastructure and automation segments contributed 62%, 25%
and 13% of revenue, respectively.
UBS EPS and Consensus EPS
The UBS EPS is an adjusted diluted EPS metric. It is calculated using the UBS analyst's
interpretation of earnings suitable for valuation purposes divided by the diluted number of
shares. This may differ to the way the consensus EPS metric has been calculated.
Valuation Method and Risk Statement
We base our price target on PE multiple valuation.

Delta's businesses include SPS and components for a variety of end-applications, video
displays and data networking subsystem and system products. Any changes in these end-
markets could affect our forecasts for Delta. Investment risk could increase/decrease on any
deviation from our expectations for end-market demand and competition.
Downside risks for Delta include: severe supply chain constraints; weaker-than-expected PC/
server demand; a slower-than-expected IA recovery; and a slower ramp of 5G in 2022.

underlying asset. Depending on the terms of the investment, investors could lose all or a substantial portion of their investment based on the performance of the underlying
asset. Investors could also lose their entire investment if the issuer becomes insolvent. UBS does not guarantee in any way the obligations or the financial condition of any

issuer or the accuracy of any financial information provided by any issuer. Structured investments are not traditional investments and investing in a structured investment is
not equivalent to investing directly in the underlying asset. Structured investments may have limited or no liquidity, and investors should be prepared to hold their investment
to maturity. The return of structured investments may be limited by a maximum gain, participation rate or other feature. Structured investments may include call features and,

if a structured investment is called early, investors would not earn any further return and may not be able to reinvest in similar investments with similar terms. Structured
investments include costs and fees which are generally embedded in the price of the investment. The tax treatment of a structured investment may be complex and may differ
from a direct investment in the underlying asset. UBS and its employees do not provide tax advice. Investors should consult their own tax advisor about their own tax situation

ab 15 September 2026
Global Research
First Read
Novatek Microelectronics Corp.
2026 Taiwan Summit: PC weakness offset by
continued momentum from major U.S. customer
Q3 revenue still expected to grow 5-6% QoQ despite weaker notebook demand
Novatek attended our 2026 Taiwan Summit on Sep 14th. It reiterates Q326 revenue to
grow  5-6% QoQ, supported by seasonal strength in S/M-sized DDI driven by the iPhone
ramp. SoC revenue is expected to grow slightly QoQ, while LDDI should decline

modestly as TV demand remains flattish and PC demand weakens. Importantly,
management highlights notebook PC has seen a meaningful downward adjustment
recently. While the company had originally expected NB shipments to decline  slightly
QoQ, demand has deteriorated to over 10% decline QoQ, with the impact becoming
visible since mid-August. Nevertheless, Q326F guidance for TV, tablet and automotive
remains unchanged. Looking into Q426, management expects seasonal weakness to

continue, with softer memory-driven ASP increases and lower shipment volume likely
resulting in sequential revenue decline.
GM likely peaked in Q226 and should normalize into H226 and 2027
Management highlighted that Q226 GM expanded to 42% from 39% in Q126, mainly
driven by  favourable product mix and lower-cost of  inventory for memory. Looking
ahead, GM is expected to decline QoQ in Q326F as the inventory benefit disappears and
growth shifts toward S/M-sized DDI and LDDI, which carry lower margins than SoC.

Management expects Q426 GM to further contract QoQ, driven by less favourable mix
and softer memory-driven ASP increases. Further out, memory, foundry and OSAT costs
are expected to continue rising into 2027. While Novatek expects to pass through most
cost increases, management acknowledged that the degree and timing of pass-through
will depend on the  negotiation with its customers.
Major US customer remains the key growth driver for 2027-28
The company reiterated strong visibility from its major U.S. customer and expects

revenue to further grow in 2027. Following entry into iPhone DDI programs in 2024 and
subsequent share gains in 2025-26, Novatek expects to continue benefiting from rising
market share as new iPhone models proliferate. Into 2027-28F,  iPhone-related growth
should moderate as the revenue base becomes larger, while management expects
increasing contribution from  premium LCD panels for Macs, supported by a more visible
roadmap. Beyond the U.S. customer, image SoC remains a bright spot due to strong

surveillance demand and emerging Edge AI applications, although management
acknowledged recent growth rates are unlikely to be sustained.
Valuation: Maintain NEUTRAL with price target of NT$540
We retain NEUTRAL with PT of NT$540. While we continue to expect GM normalization
in H226E and 2027E, we believe its GM should sustain at the high-30% level, rather
than  returning to pre-COVID's low-30%.

Company Description
Novatek is a IC design company spun off from UMC's commercial product division in 1997.
The company is focusing on the analog and mixed signal IC design and leads in the display
driver IC and TV SoC market.
Valuation Method and Risk Statement
We value Novatek using a PE methodology.

Upside risks include stronger-than-expected demand for the consumer electronics end-
market, as well as higher market share for OLED DDI.
Downside risks include a weaker-than-expected technology end-market demand recovery
and slower-than-expected inventory digestion.

KEY DEFINITIONS:Forecast Stock Return (FSR) is defined as expected percentage price appreciation plus gross dividend yield over
the next 12 months. In some cases, this yield may be based on accrued dividends. Market Return Assumption (MRA) is defined as
the one-year local market interest rate plus 5% (a proxy for, and not a forecast of, the equity risk premium). Under Review (UR)
Stocks may be flagged as UR by the analyst, indicating that the stock's price target and/or rating are subject to possible change in the

near term, usually in response to an event that may affect the investment case or valuation. Equity Price Targets have an investment
horizon of 12 months.

Investing in structured investments involves significant risks. For a detailed discussion of the risks involved in investing in any particular structured investment, you must read

the relevant offering materials for that investment. Structured investments are unsecured obligations of a particular issuer with returns linked to the performance of an
underlying asset. Depending on the terms of the investment, investors could lose all or a substantial portion of their investment based on the performance of the underlying
asset. Investors could also lose their entire investment if the issuer becomes insolvent. UBS does not guarantee in any way the obligations or the financial condition of any

issuer or the accuracy of any financial information provided by any issuer. Structured investments are not traditional investments and investing in a structured investment is
not equivalent to investing directly in the underlying asset. Structured investments may have limited or no liquidity, and investors should be prepared to hold their investment
to maturity. The return of structured investments may be limited by a maximum gain, participation rate or other feature. Structured investments may include call features and,

if a structured investment is called early, investors would not earn any further return and may not be able to reinvest in similar investments with similar terms. Structured
investments include costs and fees which are generally embedded in the price of the investment. The tax treatment of a structured investment may be complex and may differ
from a direct investment in the underlying asset. UBS and its employees do not provide tax advice. Investors should consult their own tax advisor about their own tax situation

before investing in any securities.

Powertech T echnology
2026 T aiwan Summit: FOPLP to see more
revenue contribution from 2027F
FOPLP business supported by AMD and Broadcom
PTI attended our T aiwan Summit on Sep 14th. Management noted its  FOPLP capacity in
T aiwan will be at 6K substrate/month (3K in 2026 and add another 3K in 2027 with full
ramp in 2028) with panel substrate size of 510 mm x 515 mm. Management noted  most
of the capacity in T aiwan is allocated to AMD, which it will start from the  game-console

products and then target to enter server CPU. For the Broadcom business, PTI has
previously announced a JV with Broadcom in Singapore, where it will invest US$400mn
into the JV for 30% stake, after receiving regulatory approvals in Q426. The JV will focus
on Broadcom's next generation networking products and will help it to enter into optical
communication field.  It has not disclosed the total investment amount and planned
capacity for the Singapore JV fab, but we believe the planned capacity  could be 2-3x

versus its scale in T aiwan. The JV is expected to start mass production from 2028 and PTI
will be in charged of the fab operations. Nevertheless, PTI also acknowledges that
TSMC's CoPoS will not only lead to potential competition, but could  also have some
impact on the equipment supply schedule.
Memory-backed price hike should continue
PTI's August sales of NT$8,558mn was up 3.5% MoM and 24.5% YoY. QTD sales is
tracking to 69%/68% of UBSe/Street estimates of +5%/+6% QoQ. Management noted

its  back-end loading is already at 90% and it has been selective on customer programs
for better ASP products. Management also expects back-end ASP should continue to
increase, driven primarily by higher labor costs and rising component prices. At the same
time, the pressure to lower its ASPs and  share the profit from yield improvement has
eased. Relative to peers, PTI noted it has been less aggressive in implementing price
increases, but has increased the frequency of price negotiation with its customer. As a

result, its gross margin for  memory packaging and test should continue to trend higher
in the coming quarters.
Capex will remain elevated in 2026-27F
Management reiterate its 2026F capex guidance of NT$50bn and believes its capex in
2027F will remain elevated. It aims to use its internal cash flow and bank loans to
support the capex, and remains committed to keep its  dividend payout at ~60%. Full
year  revenue for 2026F is likely to surpass its prior peak in 2022 (i.e. NT$83.9bn),

although it believes  market expectation of NT$100bn in 2026E could be too stretched.
Valuation: Retain NEUTRAL with PT of NT$260
We retain NEUTRAL on PTI with PT of NT$260, based on 17x 2027 PE. We will continue
to monitor its progress on FOPLP/CPO and price improvement sustainability.

underlying asset. Depending on the terms of the investment, investors could lose all or a substantial portion of their investment based on the performance of the underlying
asset. Investors could also lose their entire investment if the issuer becomes insolvent. UBS does not guarantee in any way the obligations or the financial condition of any

issuer or the accuracy of any financial information provided by any issuer. Structured investments are not traditional investments and investing in a structured investment is
not equivalent to investing directly in the underlying asset. Structured investments may have limited or no liquidity, and investors should be prepared to hold their investment
to maturity. The return of structured investments may be limited by a maximum gain, participation rate or other feature. Structured investments may include call features and,

if a structured investment is called early, investors would not earn any further return and may not be able to reinvest in similar investments with similar terms. Structured
investments include costs and fees which are generally embedded in the price of the investment. The tax treatment of a structured investment may be complex and may differ
from a direct investment in the underlying asset. UBS and its employees do not provide tax advice. Investors should consult their own tax advisor about their own tax situation

## Document 103: 260917_ms_CCL

Source PDF: all report pdf/260917_ms_CCL.pdf

### Page 1

Greater China Technology Hardware
Asia Pacific
Industry View In-Line
What’s new? EMC (2383.TW) shares fell 7.7% and TUC (6274.TWO) shares declined
6.7% on Sep 17, vs TAIEX +0.8%. Following the sell-off, investors have questioned
whether CPO could disrupt demand for high-end CCL. The concern is that
integrating optical engines alongside the ASIC on the package substrate shortens
high-speed electrical signal paths that would otherwise traverse the printed circuit

board (PCB), potentially reducing the need for ultra-low-Dk/Df, high-speed CCL.
Our thoughts:  This is not a new debate. We previously discussed the potential
implications of CPO for high-speed CCL demand here and here.  We believe this is
particularly relevant for scale-up architectures, where CPO adoption still faces
meaningful challenges related to cost, manufacturing yield, reliability, serviceability,
and thermal management. As such, we believe the risk of a broad-based reduction in

CCL requirements across AI systems before 2028 remains limited.  We would view
CPO-driven pullbacks in CCL stocks as potential opportunities to accumulate.
Morgan Stanley does and seeks to do business with

Key Takeaways
Co-packaged optics (CPO) is a long-term risk, not an imminent demand
disruption.
While we agree that broader CPO adoption represents a credible longer-term risk
to premium copper-clad laminate (CCL) content, we see limited risk to the
demand outlook over 2026–28.
We see limited near-term impact on CCL demand or our earnings estimates for

EMC and TUC, leaving our premium-CCL supply-tightness thesis and constructive
fundamental view intact.

Equal-weight (E). The stock's total return is expected to be in line with the average total return of the analyst's industry (or industry team's) coverage universe, on a risk-adjusted basis, over

Not-Rated (NR). Currently the analyst does not have adequate conviction about the stock's total return relative to the average total return of the analyst's industry (or industry team's) coverage
universe, on a risk-adjusted basis, over the next 12-18 months.

12-18 months.

ab 18 September 2026
Global Research
Nanya Technology
Pricing reset driving upside in 3Q
3Q26 tracking well ahead of consensus
Nanya Tech's July ’26 revs were up 49% MoM and August 2%. Combined, July+August
is equivalent to 80% of VA consensus 3Q revenue of NT$111bn. We understand this
comes from both DRAM bit shipments and ASP upside. We now forecast QoQ bits up
5% vs -8% prior. More noticeably, we now forecast DRAM ASPs up 50% QoQ (vs.
+32% prior). We believe this comes from some 6-month to 1-year contracts which re-

set last July, leading to well above average QoQ pricing momentum. Also, with niche
DRAM exposure and less concentration around large clients, Nanya’s DRAM ASPs are
edging higher than its much larger peers as the upcycle continues. Looking into 4Q26,
we forecast ASPs to increase 10% QoQ. With that, gross margin should improve in
3Q26 to 86.1% from 79.5% in 2Q, and remain at elevated levels throughout 2027.
Reiterate Buy.
Not fulfilling customers’ demand until the next fab ramps

Nanya sees 50-60% fulfillment rate for demand currently. Several large customers are
not getting any allocation. Long term agreements cover >60% of bits already. Its new
fab will start equipment moving-in in 1Q27, with initial output in 3Q27. Initial capacity
will reach 30k wpm by 2028, with total theoretical capacity of 45-50k wpm. Nanya is
also constructing an EUV litho building with equipment moving in in 1Q28. The goal is
to secure 2 tools with space up to 5. Up to its 1d nm (which is 1a nm equivalent), Nanya

does not require EUV litho.
Increasing forecasts
We increase 3Q26E revs/EPS estimates to NT$133bn/NT$26.44 (by 30%/40%),
20%/37% above Visible Alpha consensus of NT$110bn/NT$19.26. We also increase
2026E/2027E/2028E EPS forecasts by 23%/12%/18% respectively on higher
DRAM ASP assumptions (9%/9%/4% higher per Gb vs prior).
Valuation: PT to NT$640 from NT$555; maintain Buy
We value Nanya Tech shares at 3.16x NTM P/BV (was 3.01x) based on our LT
ROE estimate of 26.5% (was 25.5%) and CoE of 8.4% (was 8.5%).

### Page 2

Nanya Technology 18 September 2026 ab 2
Nanya Technology UBS ResearchNanya Tech (2408.TW)
Thesis Map     UBS                    Research     THESIS MAP a guide to our thinking and what´s where in this report
Q: Will DRAM undersupply continue into 2028?
Yes in our view. Agentic AI is boosting further memory demand on multiple fronts beyond HBM,
including DDR5/LPDDR5 for conventional servers and CPU head nodes in AI servers. We now forecast
an acceleration of memory demand growth into 2027 with DRAM bit end-consumption growing

40% YoY vs 21% in 2026. As almost all of the incremental wafer capacity addition for DRAM is
going to HBM, supply is not catching up with demand. The main risk remains affordability by
customers as memory industry revenues are expected to reach US$1.64tn in 2027E.
Q: Can NTC grow as a niche DRAM player?
Yes. 2026 and 2027 are likely to be years of more constrained growth. Subsequently though, we
think its process tech migration to 1c nm and 1d nm will likely lead to a 30% increase in bits per wafer

for each process tech migration (at comparable yields). NTC is also slightly pulling in its new fab ramp,
with equipment expected to move in 1Q27. We also see a tail of DDR3 and DDR4 products NTC can
address for a while.
Nanya Tech shares trade at 2.59x NTM P/BV, above +1SD of its 10-year average. That said, we believe
the strength of the unfolding DRAM cycle as well as the tail of legacy products that Nanya can
address as a niche player should continue to provide support for the stock.

Our industry checks suggest HBM demand continues to result in capacity allocation away from DDR,
which may moderate possible cyclical corrections, supporting upside to DDR contract pricing for
longer.
At 2.59x NTM P/BV, we believe Nanya Tech shares are discounting a LT average ROE of 21.7% vs our
LT estimate of 26.5%.

Company Description
Nanya Tech is a pure DRAM company based in Taiwan, focusing on legacy products for
consumers, broad-based applications and is now growing in servers.
Valuation Method and Risk Statement
Nanya Tech is a pure-play DRAM manufacturer based in Taiwan mainly focused on legacy DDR

products for customers across various end applications. We think downside risks to our thesis
could include a potential slowdown in end demand and hence the conventional memory
cycle as well as Nanya's legacy-centric product portfolio. We value Nanya Tech shares using a
target NTM P/BV multiple based on long-term average ROE and cost of equity.

underlying asset. Depending on the terms of the investment, investors could lose all or a substantial portion of their investment based on the performance of the underlying
asset. Investors could also lose their entire investment if the issuer becomes insolvent. UBS does not guarantee in any way the obligations or the financial condition of any

issuer or the accuracy of any financial information provided by any issuer. Structured investments are not traditional investments and investing in a structured investment is
not equivalent to investing directly in the underlying asset. Structured investments may have limited or no liquidity, and investors should be prepared to hold their investment
to maturity. The return of structured investments may be limited by a maximum gain, participation rate or other feature. Structured investments may include call features and,

if a structured investment is called early, investors would not earn any further return and may not be able to reinvest in similar investments with similar terms. Structured
investments include costs and fees which are generally embedded in the price of the investment. The tax treatment of a structured investment may be complex and may differ
from a direct investment in the underlying asset. UBS and its employees do not provide tax advice. Investors should consult their own tax advisor about their own tax situation

before investing in any securities.

Coherent Corp (COHR.K)
21 September 2026 Citi Research

Strategy and positioning: Management launched PhotonLink as an architecture-
agnostic integrated optics platform covering CPO, NPO, and chip-to-chip optical
connections. It spans the full optical chain: Generating the light, shaping and
guiding it, and detecting it at the far end. Management discussed that its
customers asked it to supply complete assemblies rather than individual
components as stitching together lasers, fiber and passive optics is difficult. It

argued that no other company holds the full portfolio in-house and that Coherent
can manufacture at datacenter scale. Management expects a mix of adoption
paths, with some customers going straight to CPO and others starting with NPO
and moving to CPO later.
Figure 1. COHR's Portfolio of Optical AI Networking Products
Source: COHR at ECOC
Customers and content: In a full-solution example (combining the ELS, the
assembly to the switch or XPU, and the assembly out to the faceplate),

management said Coherent content could reach up to $15k of content per
switch/processor chip needing 100T of I/O capacity at 200G optical lane. Coherent
counts more than 10 customer engagements each in CPO and NPO and more than
5 in chip-to-chip, with activity going up sharply over the past six months. For CPO,
management said it has an anchor customer with an LTA secured, which it
identified as NVDA. It also has an anchor customer and LTA for NPO, which it did

not name. Separately, management cited two LTAs for ultra-high-power CW lasers
with leading hyperscale or AI datacenter customers, also unnamed.

### Page 3

Coherent Corp (COHR.K)
21 September 2026 Citi Research
3
Figure 2. PhontonLink Platform
Source: COHR at ECOC 2026
Timing: CPO for scale-out, tied to the NVIDIA agreement, begins ramping in the
December quarter (calendar Q4 2026). CPO for scale-up follows in the second half
of calendar 2027. NPO ramps in the second half of next calendar year, mainly for
scale-up. Chip-to-chip is further out, around 2029-2030.
Light generation: The ultra-high-power CW laser sits in an external laser source

that holds up to eight lasers, each feeding roughly four links. It starts ramping this
quarter, with significant volume next year, on the 6-inch InP platform in Sherman,
Texas. For NPO, a high-power buried-heterostructure CW laser is already shipping
in millions of units per month for pluggables. VCSEL arrays come in a conventional
version for ribbon fiber and a high-density 2D version that can be flip-chipped
directly to drivers and TIAs with backside lenses. Photodetectors run to 200G

today, with 400G in development.
Figure 3. UHP CW Laser Leader
Source: COHR at ECOC 2026

### Page 4

Coherent Corp (COHR.K)
21 September 2026 Citi Research
4
Fab footprint: Sherman runs 6-inch InP and GaAs, Sweden runs 6-inch InP . Zurich
runs 6-inch GaAs and is adding 6-inch InP for high-power lasers, while Fremont
runs a 3-inch line. GaAs capacity has grown fourfold since the 6-inch move about
six years ago, with capacity for over one billion VCSEL arrays per year. InP capacity
doubled last year, a quarter ahead of schedule, and management plans to double it

again or more.
Figure 4. COHR Capacity Expansion
Source: COHR at ECOC 2026
Shape, guide, and receive: Coherent grows garnet in the United States and says it
supplies a significant fraction of the industry's garnet and isolators, with
customers signing LTAs for capacity. The ELS is built on the transceiver line and is
sampling now. The rest of the portfolio covers specialty fiber (polarization-
maintaining fiber production-ready, mode-matched fiber introduced at ECOC,

multi-core fiber), micro-lens arrays, V-grooves, fiber array units, a detachable
connector, circulators, WDM multiplexers, and fiber shuffles.
Silicon photonics and engines: Management discussed Coherent having an in-
house silicon photonics design team, uses foundries for wafers, and does assembly
and test in-house. It ships 200G-per-lane silicon photonics in transceivers today
and showed a 400G link at OFC with a post-deadline paper. It has a 6.4T silicon

photonics NPO module (32 lanes of 200G) and a VCSEL-based NPO with 2D
arrays, which management says achieves about 1.2 pJ/bit including the laser.
Architecture trade-off: Management said NPO is easier to deploy and service but
costs power and signal integrity versus CPO, and that a common NPO socket can
take silicon photonics or VCSELs. It positioned Coherent as an honest advisor
because it can compare all the options. Chip-to-chip is a growing topic, with WDM

and circulators important there.

Key takeaways from Citi discussion with management:
What is Coherent's competitive advantage in 3.2T, and will it participate?
Management said it has already demonstrated the building blocks for the 3.2T
generation, including 400G-per-lane EMLs and 400G silicon photonics, and
expects to participate just as it enables 1.6T today. Management showed these

demonstrations as early as two years ago.
What is the gross margin path, and what offsets mix pressure? Management
mentioned that the 42%+ target was deliberately open-ended and that it expects
to exceed it. It cautioned against expecting a step change over the next two to
three quarters. Fast transceiver growth is a mix headwind, offset by overhead
absorption, yield gains and factory consolidation. Management expects the 800G-
to-1.6T transition to be margin-accretive, with the cutover forecast around 2028.

### Page 6

Coherent Corp (COHR.K)
21 September 2026 Citi Research
6
OCS, shipping for two to three quarters, is the first of the new platforms to
generate revenue. OCS, CPO and multi-rail will contribute more to margins as mix
builds.
What are the challenges and economics of the 6-inch InP transition?
Management said it announced 6-inch capability in March 2024 after years of
work with substrate vendors that began before the AI boom. Output is expected to
be roughly 50/50 between 3-inch and 6-inch by the end of the quarter, with all

incremental capacity on 6-inch, reaching about 75% by the end of 2027. A 6-inch
die costs about half as much per yielded die, and each line delivers about four
times the capacity. Yields are better on modern tooling. Management cited a three-
to-four-year lead over competitors and secured substrate supply from five
suppliers across three continents. It also credited its 6-inch GaAs VCSEL line to a
large consumer-electronics customer that demanded the larger wafer size.

Will Coherent keep external InP suppliers? COHR only sources EMLs externally
and that it will keep some external supply for continuity on a critical component.
How does Coherent differ from Chinese laser suppliers? Management argued
that module assembly is easier to replicate but high-speed lasers are not. It said
there are no high-speed EMLs or broadband tunable lasers from China, and that
Chinese CW lasers top out around 70-100 mW. It sees only one InP laser

competitor worth naming and expects new Chinese module entrants to take share
from existing Chinese suppliers rather than from Coherent.
Does NPO vs CPO matter for content, and can low-power lasers serve NPO?
Management said it does not matter much, because the components and dollar
content are similar. Designs are custom and take 18 to 24 months to reach volume,
and management reiterated scale-up production revenue in the second half of next
year. Management rejected the view that NPO can use low-power lasers, arguing

that coupling several weak lasers loses light and defeats the power-efficiency
purpose.
What is multi-rail, and how is it progressing? Multi-rail addresses scale-across
links between data centers. Management said it delivers four times the capacity in
the same footprint at roughly 30% lower power per lane, enabled by a multi-chip
uncooled pump that it says has no comparable competitor. Small shipments are
underway and production shipments begin in the first half of next calendar year. It

sells at the component, module, line-card and system level, including white-label
to OEMs.

Coherent Corp
Company description
COHR is a vertically integrated manufacturing company that develops
engineered materials and opto-electronic components for industrial
materials processing, communications, aerospace and defense, consumer
electronics, semiconductor capital equipment, life sciences and automotive
end markets. COHR produces a wide variety of application-specific photonic
and electronic materials and components, and deploys them in various forms,

including integration with advanced software. COHR's customer base
includes original equipment manufacturers, laser end users, system
integrators of high-power lasers, manufacturers of equipment and devices for
industrial, optical communications, consumer electronics, security and
monitoring applications, U.S. government prime contractors, and various U.S.
government agencies. COHR is a headquartered in Pennsylvania.
Investment strategy
We are Buy-rated on COHR. We believe that the stock's multiple will benefit

from the AI appeal while its fundamentals should expand on new
management's strong execution and focus on profitability.
Valuation
We value COHR at $420 or 30x forward P/E applied to FY2028 EPS of ~$16
discounted back. Our COHR valuation is nevertheless at a 10% discount to
the average forward P/E of AI optics peers to reflect a lower AI sales mix and
3-year EPS CAGR vs peers such as LITE.
Risks
Downside risks to the achievement of our target price include: 1) increased

competition on AI and SiC leads to limited market share growth and limited
revenue upside, 2) inability to achieve synergies and margin targets
established post acquisition of Finisar, and 3) prolonged economic recession
leads to slower 5G build-out and lower consumer demand driving revenue of
COHR down.
Upside risks to the achievement of our target price include: 1) gaining share in
AI and SiC market through new product offerings and first to market status

on larger wafer sizes, 2) quicker and stronger adoption of AI workloads,
electric and autonomous vehicles, and 3) quicker return of margins to pre-
Finisar acquisition levels.

Guide to Citi Research Fundamental Research Investment Ratings:
Citi Research stock recommendations include an investment rating and an optional risk rating to highlight high risk stocks.

Risk rating takes into account both price volatility and fundamental criteria. Stocks will either have no risk rating or a High risk
rating assigned.
Investment Ratings: Citi Research investment ratings are Buy, Neutral and Sell. Our ratings are a function of analyst
expectations of expected total return ("ETR") and risk. ETR is the sum of the forecast price appreciation (or depreciation) plus
the dividend yield for a stock within the next 12 months.  The target price is based on a 12 month time horizon. The Investment

rating definitions are: Buy (1) ETR of 15% or more or 25% or more for High risk stocks; and Sell (3) for negative ETR. Any covered
stock not assigned a Buy or a Sell is a Neutral (2). For stocks rated Neutral (2), if an analyst believes that there are insufficient
valuation drivers and/or investment catalysts to derive a positive or negative investment view, they may elect with the approval
of Citi Research management not to assign a target price and, thus, not derive an ETR. Citi Research may suspend its rating

and target price and assign “Rating Suspended” status for regulatory and/or internal policy reasons. Citi Research may also
suspend its rating and target price and assign "Under Review" status for other exceptional circumstances (e.g. lack of
information critical to the analyst's thesis, trading suspension) affecting the company and/or trading in the company's
securities. In both such situations, the rating and target price will show as “—“ and “-“ respectively in the rating history price

chart. Prior to 11 April 2022 Citi Research assigned “Under Review” status to both situations and prior to 11 Nov 2020 only in
exceptional circumstances. As soon as practically possible, the analyst will publish a note re-establishing a rating and
investment thesis. Investment ratings are determined by the ranges described above at the time of initiation of coverage, a
change in investment and/or risk rating, or a change in target price (subject to limited management discretion). At times, the

expected total returns may fall outside of these ranges because of market price movements and/or other short-term volatility
or trading patterns. Such interim deviations will be permitted but will become subject to review by Research Management.
Your decision to buy or sell a security should be based upon your personal investment objectives and should be made only
after evaluating the stock's expected performance and risk.

Update
E Ink Holdings Inc.  | Asia Pacific
Read-across from Vusion's 2Q26
Earnings Call
Positive implications for E Ink from Vusion's comments on strong
order entries into 2H26 with further acceleration in 4Q26. But
with no strong catalyst in sight, we stay EW despite trough level
valuations.
What's new:
• VusionGroup (VU.PA, Not Covered), one of the major system integrators for
electronic shelf label (ESL) systems, reported its 1H26 audited results (see

here for read-across from its 2Q26 sales).
• By region, growth in 1H26 was mostly driven by America and improving
momentum in Europe. For EMEA, momentum was good with revenue and
order intakes growing. Management expects higher growth and more project
wins in 2H26, in the grocery sector and other verticals, and targets 15-20% of
growth in 2H26. For Americas, it sees strong pipeline with major North and
South American retailers, thus also anticipates  good momentum into 2H26

and strong future adoption in coming years.
• Management reiterated its 2026 guidance of 15-20% YoY (excluding the FX
and tariff impacts). It aims to grow VAS revenue by ~ 40% YoY to reach
~20% of its total revenue in 2026 (guided to rise to 30% in 2027).
• On order entries, Vusion management targets over €1bn in 2H26, with new
flows increasing over the coming months leading to a particularly strong
4Q26. It believes these could further fuel growth into 2027.

• It maintained the sales target of €2.2bn for 2027, driven by existing/new
customers, new solutions and broadened geographies. In the longer term, it
believes topline growth will be driven by increasing penetration of ESL (from
20% now to 50%) and VAS (which is more under-penetrated vs. ESL).  This is
despite the strong revenue growth in 2025-26 pulling in some momentum
from 2028-29.
Our view:
• Positive comments from Vusion on the robust order entries into 2H26 and

more deployment in the retail media are consistent with E Ink's view on the
solid ESL and signage demand for the year.
• That said, we think E Ink's CE business will remain a drag.
• Despite E Ink's trough valuation at 12x 2027e P/E and our belief in e-paper
demand in various applications, we see no strong catalysts in the near term,
and stay EW.

Valuation Methodology and Risks
E Ink Holdings Inc. (8069.TWO)
Base case, 12x 2027e P/E. We believe this valuation methodology best captures E Ink's earn-
ings growth momentum. We view our target multiple of 12x as fair, considering our estimated
17% earnings CAGR for 2025-28. The implied PEG of 0.7x is largely in line with its typical level
in 2022-25, when the stock was trading at an average P/E of 22x one-year forward consensus
EPS with a 37% earnings CAGR.

Risks to Upside
n Firmer-than-expected ESL orders
n Stronger demand for e-readers and e-notes
n Better macro conditions
n Milder competition
n Brisker inventory digestion
Risks to Downside
n Softer-than-expected ESL orders
n Slower demand for e-readers and e-notes
n Macro headwinds
n Intensified competition
n More protracted inventory digestion

Equal-weight (E). The stock's total return is expected to be in line with the average total return of the analyst's industry (or industry team's) coverage universe, on a risk-adjusted basis, over

the next 12-18 months.
Not-Rated (NR). Currently the analyst does not have adequate conviction about the stock's total return relative to the average total return of the analyst's industry (or industry team's) coverage
universe, on a risk-adjusted basis, over the next 12-18 months.
Underweight (U). The stock's total return is expected to be below the average total return of the analyst's industry (or industry team's) coverage universe, on a risk-adjusted basis, over the next

12-18 months.
Unless otherwise specified, the time frame for price targets included in Morgan Stanley Research is 12 to 18 months.
Analyst Industry Views
Attractive (A): The analyst expects the performance of his or her industry coverage universe over the next 12-18 months to be attractive vs. the relevant broad market benchmark, as indicated
below.
In-Line (I): The analyst expects the performance of his or her industry coverage universe over the next 12-18 months to be in line with the relevant broad market benchmark, as indicated below.

Cautious (C): The analyst views the performance of his or her industry coverage universe over the next 12-18 months with caution vs. the relevant broad market benchmark, as indicated below.

## Document 120: 260922_ubs_GUC

Source PDF: all report pdf/260922_ubs_GUC.pdf

### Page 1

ab 22 September 2026
Global Research
Global Unichip
Better wafer allocation and demand upside
driving H226-2027E earnings growth
Better wafter allocation driving H226-2027E CPU project ramps
We expect CPU projects to remain GUC's main revenue driver in 2026-27E and see
improved wafer allocation into 2027E. We now expect Google CPU volumes to ramp
from 1.3mn units in 2026E to ~4mn units in 2027E, supported by rising TPU shipments
(up 117% YoY in 2027E), a rising CPU-to-TPU ratio, and better wafer allocation from

TSMC. Although GUC's CPU projects carry lower GM, we believe they remain earnings
accretive given the operating leverage from limited incremental OPEX requirements. We
now expect 2026E revenue growth of 94% YoY to NT$66.3 bn (vs prior +90% YoY) and
2027E revenue to grow 146% YoY (with Google CPU contributing 67% of 2027E sales),
up from our prior estimate of 84% YoY. We also expect OPM to expand from 13.2% in
2026E to 13.9% in 2028E. Accordingly, we raise our 2027/28E EPS estimates by

29%/22% and lift our PT to NT$8,660 (from NT$6,700), based on 52x average 2027-
28E EPS. Our 2027/28E EPS estimates are 23%/14% above consensus.
Broadening CSP exposure supports medium-term growth
Beyond the Google CPU ramp, we also see improving demand from Microsoft's Maia
platform, where GUC supplies CPU and the Maia 200 accelerator. Although Maia 300 is
shifting to another supplier, we see extended runway for Maia 200, as well as continued
CPU shipments into 2027E. For the next-gen Maia 400, we believe this remains in the

bidding stage, with GUC maintaining a competitive position over peers. GUC also
secured a 2nm ASIC project from Meta in Q226 for a turnkey revenue ramp from mid-
2028E. These CPU and ASIC projects, along with GUC's strong execution track record,
provide attractive opportunities to engage with top CSPs on accelerator opportunities.
Nevertheless, we do not expect meaningful revenue contribution before 2028.
Automotive to see more significant contribution from mid-2027E

We believe automotive will be another key growth driver for GUC over the medium
term, initially supported by a Chinese EV customer from late-2026, followed by a US EV
maker in H227E. We estimate automotive will contribute 2%/13% of total revenue in
2026E/27E, respectively, increasing further to 18% in 2028E. As GUC offers higher
value-add in the automotive projects vs. Google CPU, we believe they should support
GM and deliver a higher profit contribution relative to sales. In addition, revenue could

see further upside should these solutions expand into robotic applications.
Valuation: Retain BUY, raise PT to NT$8,660
Our NT$8,660 price target is based on 52x average 2027-28E EPS (vs prior 50x), vs
historical 17-84x range, supported by 56% CAGR in earnings over 2025-30E. We
reiterate our Buy rating, as GUC is well positioned for upside in CPU demand, ramp of
automotive projects, other ASICs and emerging optical interconnect opportunities.

Global Unichip UBS ResearchGlobal Unichip (3443.TW)
Thesis Map     UBS                    Research     THESIS MAP a guide to our thinking and what´s where in this report
Q: Can GUC further grow its AI and high-performance computing sales?
Yes, in our view, supported by multiple drivers. GUC has benefited from being part of TSMC's
ecosystem, with better access to TSMC's technology roadmap, especially on advanced nodes. It has
won several CPU/XPU projects from US hyperscalers and it is also working with leading EV makers on

next-generation autonomous driving ASICs. GUC aims to expand its tier-1 hyperscaler customer base
and we believe there is an opportunity for it to provide advanced packaging services, leveraging the
CoWoS capacity it secured, even though it is not directly involved in the ASIC design.
Q: Are GUC's projects on mature nodes (16nm and above) sustainable?
We think they are likely to remain stable. GUC's customers are sticky on 16nm and higher nodes.
Owing to its strong IP portfolio, which reduces design costs and improves manufacturing yield, these

mature nodes still contribute around 30% of GUC's sales in 2025. While we expect mature nodes to
remain accretive to margins – catering to repeat projects that require little R&D resources – the
growth is likely to be modest at 27% CAGR for 2025-28E vs 104% CAGR for advanced nodes.
Q: Will GUC's OPM recover in 2026-28?
We expect its OPM to show a slight improvement in 2026, as it further ramps the lower-GM Google
CPU project, and incurs a temporary increase in opex due to the new Turing centre. However, we

foresee a more significant improvement in OPM from 2027 as it ramps a higher GM autonomous
driving project from H227, growing  NRE contributions, and restocking of mature projects.
We reiterate our Buy rating on GUC and raise our 2026/27/28E EPS by 0.4%/29%/22%, respectively,
primarily reflecting higher sales contributions from Google's CPU projects. We raise our price target
from NT$6,700 to NT$8,660 based on 52x average 2027-28E EPS (vs a 17-84x historical range),

supported by a 2025-30E EPS CAGR of 56%. Potential catalysts include: 1) further TPU/CPU upside
from the Google project; 2) the continued ramp of Microsoft's AI CPU/ASIC chips and the potential to
win back future-gen projects; 3) upside on new 2nm project wins; 4) a faster ramp of autonomous EV
projects; and 5) advanced NRE opportunities with higher dollar content.
GUC's revenue remained muted in 2023-24, as it shifted its resources from Chinese to US customers

due to BIS export controls. The customer diversification effort began bearing fruit in H125, as GUC
recorded a notable uptick in the turnkey sales to US crypto customers, while the Google CPU ramp
since late Q425 appears sustainable. With the support of its major shareholder TSMC, which has
enabled better access to advanced technology, GUC continues to work with Microsoft, Tesla and
other hyperscalers on custom AI chipsets, which should underpin its  growth in the next few years.

GUC stock rallied 57% in the past three months vs 3% for the TAIEX, on Google TPU news in our
view, and is now trading at 55x 2027E EPS vs its historical 17-84x range. We believe the stock should
continue to re-rate on TPU upside, rising CPU/TPU ratio, multiple automotive project ramps, and
potential upside from wafer allocation. We expect  a 56% CAGR in earnings over 2025-30E and
foresee potential upward revisions in consensus earnings estimates being a catalyst.

Risk to the current share price is skewed (1.7:1) to the upside
GUC is trading at NT$7,615 (as of 21 September 2026).

UPSIDE (NT$12,000.00): Our upside scenario factors in stronger sales growth in 2027-
28E than we forecast in our base case, on the back of better demand for Google's TPU
and US/China automotive projects, more N3 wafer allocation by leading foundries, and
faster penetration of other hyperscalers, lifting 2027/28E sales by 170%/40% YoY. Our
upside OPM assumptions are 13.4%/14.1% for 2027/28E, 0.2ppt above our base case
owing to a limited increase in opex, supporting a 96% CAGR in earnings over 2026-28E.

Our upside scenario valuation of NT$12,000.00 implies a 76x 2027E PE.
BASE (NT$8,660.00): Our base case reflects our expectations of a solid business growth
outlook in 2027-28E, supported by the continued ramp of Google's CPU project, initial
ramp of automotive projects from Q426, and expansion into other hyperscalers. We
forecast 2027/28E sales to grow 146%/34% YoY, and OPM to expand to 13.2%/13.9%
from 12.7% in 2025 on operating leverage, despite its GM potentially normalising to

around 17.8% in 2028 (from 24.8% in 2025) on a higher proportion of sales from the
CPU project, resulting in earnings growth of 83% CAGR over 2026-28E. Our base-case
valuation of NT$8,660.00 implies a 52x 2027-28E average PE.
DOWNSIDE (NT$5,000.00): Our downside scenario factors in slower sales growth in
2027/28E than we forecast in our base case, due to softer growth in Google's CPU due to
a wafer capacity constraint and slower demand for mature process products, dampening

sales growth to 121%/26% YoY. Our downside OPM assumptions are 13.0%/13.7% for
2027/28E, 0.2pp below our base case, resulting in earnings growth decelerating to a
68% CAGR over 2026-28E. Our downside scenario valuation of NT$5,000.00 implies a
41x 2027E P/E.

Company Description
Global Unichip (GUC) is a leading IC design service company in Taiwan, founded in 1998. The
company's business is to design chipsets for customers that do not have IC design capability,
with the goal of reducing entry barriers and risks for chipset design and shortening the time

to market. The company's target to enable more IC design for start-ups and system
companies is complimentary with TSMC, which would benefit from a growing customer and
application base, in addition to the company's existing IC design and IDM customers.
Valuation Method and Risk Statement
We value Global Unichip based on a PE methodology.
Downside risks include a slower-than-expected business recovery for mature nodes, lack of
new project wins, and wafer capacity constraints.

asset. Investors could also lose their entire investment if the issuer becomes insolvent. UBS does not guarantee in any way the obligations or the financial condition of any

issuer or the accuracy of any financial information provided by any issuer. Structured investments are not traditional investments and investing in a structured investment is
